timeline.what: throwaway kit: 5 synthetic pupils in class 3B, one project each
someone signs in as s03 from the attacker's address, downloads s03's data, makes an API token and reads projects with it
the audit log shows sign-in activity and a data download for s03 from an address never seen before
sessions ended, account switched off and on again (its API tokens are deleted), password reset
audit events of the incident exported
risk assessed and notification decided (rehearsed by the maintainers; a real decision is the controller's and the DPO's)

assessment.data: one pupil's account details (username, email, class), notice records, own projects and the audit events about them; no other pupil's data; no password or token in clear
assessment.consequences: the pupil's email and school class known to an unauthorised person; their games read
assessment.risk: risk (not high): a minor's contact details and school class disclosed; contained within minutes
assessment.notify_authority: yes, within 72 hours of T0 (2026-10-24T18:26:54+00:00), because a minor's data was disclosed and the risk is not unlikely
assessment.tell_the_person: Art. 34 not required (not high risk); the school's policy is to tell the pupil and family anyway, with what to do (new password, watch for phishing)
measures: consider: alert on sign-ins from new addresses (finding F-2)

findings.finding: Local sign-ins were not in the audit log before this work; added (login, login_failed with the address, never the typed text)
No alert on sign-ins from a new address: detection relies on someone reading the audit log
Ordinary reads of projects are not audited (S-5): the extent of what an API token read is inferred from its scope and last_used
Contacts in the playbook are blank until the controller fills them in (D-10)
